questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.text: A remote pilot wants to fly an sUAS over a group of non-participant bystanders at an outdoor event without obtaining a waiver. The pilot believes the aircraft may qualify as Category 1. Under 14 CFR Part 107, what maximum weight must the sUAS meet to qualify for a Category 1 operation over people?

answers.text: The sUAS must weigh 0.55 pounds or less, including everything onboard at the time of operation
The sUAS must weigh less than 2 pounds total including all components and any attached payload
The sUAS must weigh 1 pound or less when measured without any detachable payload attached
The sUAS must weigh less than 55 pounds and have an FAA-accepted Declaration of Compliance

explanations.a: Under 14 CFR 107.115, a Category 1 operation is authorized when the sUAS weighs 0.55 pounds or less, including everything onboard at the time of the operation.
explanations.b: 2 pounds is not the Category 1 threshold; the limit is 0.55 pounds, which is also the Part 48 registration trigger weight.
explanations.c: The 0.55-pound weight is measured with all components installed during the operation, not without payload; removing payload to reclassify the aircraft misapplies the rule.
explanations.d: A Declaration of Compliance is required for Category 2 and 3 operations, not Category 1; the 55-pound figure is the overall Part 107 applicability limit.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.keyword: Category 1 no exposed laceration rotating parts
questions.text: A lightweight sUAS weighs 0.40 pounds and easily satisfies the Category 1 weight threshold. Before flying it over workers at a construction site, the remote pilot must confirm one additional design requirement. Under 14 CFR Part 107, what design characteristic must a Category 1 sUAS also satisfy?

answers.text: The sUAS must be equipped with propeller guards that are FAA-certified to withstand full-throttle blade impact
The sUAS must not contain any exposed rotating parts that would lacerate human skin upon contact with a person
The sUAS must have an automatic landing function that activates if the command signal is lost during over-people flight
The sUAS must have anti-collision lighting visible for 3 statute miles at the time of any over-people operation

explanations.a: FAA-certified propeller guards are not specified as a Category 1 requirement; the regulation focuses on whether exposed rotating parts can lacerate skin.
explanations.b: Under 14 CFR 107.115, a Category 1 sUAS must not contain any exposed rotating parts that would lacerate human skin upon contact with a person; this is the second requirement alongside the 0.55-pound weight limit.
explanations.c: An automatic landing function is not a Category 1 requirement; Part 107 Subpart D does not specify autonomous failsafe behavior for this category.
explanations.d: Anti-collision lighting is required for civil twilight and night operations under 107.29, not as a Category 1 over-people design requirement.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.text: A remote pilot plans a Category 2 sUAS operation over non-participant workers conducting exterior building maintenance. The sUAS meets the injury severity and design requirements of Category 2. Under 14 CFR Part 107, what document must the remote PIC have in their possession or readily accessible during the operation?

answers.text: A Part 107 certificate of waiver from the FAA specifically authorizing operations over non-participant human beings
A letter of authorization from the local FSDO confirming Category 2 eligibility for the specific aircraft being flown
A Declaration of Compliance indicating the sUAS satisfies the Category 2 injury severity and design standards
An FAA-issued type certificate or supplemental type certificate for the sUAS being used in the over-people operation

explanations.a: A certificate of waiver is the mechanism for deviating from Part 107 rules; it is not the standard authorization document for Category 2 over-people operations.
explanations.b: FSDO letters of authorization are not the Category 2 compliance mechanism; the Declaration of Compliance filed with the FAA DroneZone is the required document.
explanations.c: Under 14 CFR 107.120, a Category 2 operation requires the remote PIC to have a Declaration of Compliance — documenting that the sUAS meets the FAA-accepted injury severity limit and design requirements — in their possession or readily accessible.
explanations.d: Type certificates and supplemental type certificates are Part 21 airworthiness documents required for Category 4 operations, not Category 2.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.keyword: Category 2 injury severity FAA accepted limit
questions.text: A drone manufacturer is designing an sUAS to qualify for Category 2 operations over people. The engineering team asks how the FAA evaluates whether the aircraft meets the Category 2 injury severity requirement. Under 14 CFR Part 107, the Category 2 injury severity standard is based on what?

answers.text: The sUAS must produce a noise level below 65 decibels at 25 feet, which correlates with reduced impact hazard to persons
The sUAS must be rated by an independent safety laboratory as posing no more than a 1-in-1,000,000 risk of serious injury
The sUAS must weigh less than 4 pounds and travel no faster than 45 knots during any over-people segment
The sUAS must not exceed the FAA-accepted injury severity limit, which manufacturers demonstrate through a means of compliance accepted by the FAA and documented in a Declaration of Compliance

explanations.a: Noise level is not an injury severity metric under Part 107 Category 2 requirements; decibel ratings have no role in the over-people qualification process.
explanations.b: Part 107 does not use a probabilistic risk ratio as the Category 2 injury standard; the standard is an FAA-accepted injury severity limit demonstrated through accepted means of compliance.
explanations.c: A specific weight and speed combination is not the Category 2 injury severity standard; the regulation uses an FAA-accepted injury severity framework documented in the Declaration of Compliance.
explanations.d: Under 14 CFR 107.120, a Category 2 sUAS must not exceed the FAA-accepted limit for injury severity; manufacturers demonstrate compliance through an FAA-accepted means of compliance and record this in a Declaration of Compliance submitted to the FAA.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.text: A remote pilot holds a Declaration of Compliance confirming the sUAS meets Category 3 requirements. The pilot is asked to fly over a crowd attending an outdoor music festival. Under 14 CFR Part 107, may a Category 3 sUAS conduct this operation over the open-air assembly?

answers.text: Yes, if the remote pilot reduces airspeed to the minimum required for stable flight while passing over the festival crowd
No, Category 3 operations may not be conducted over an open-air assembly of human beings under any circumstance
Yes, provided each section of the crowd has a dedicated visual observer to monitor for hazards from below
Yes, as long as the sUAS altitude remains at least 400 feet above the highest person in the assembly

explanations.a: Reducing airspeed does not create a Category 3 exception for open-air assemblies; the prohibition is categorical and not speed-dependent.
explanations.b: Under 14 CFR 107.125, a Category 3 operation may not be conducted over an open-air assembly of human beings; this prohibition applies regardless of speed, altitude, or the presence of visual observers.
explanations.c: Visual observers address VLOS requirements, not the Category 3 open-air assembly prohibition; their presence does not create an exception to this rule.
explanations.d: Altitude does not create a Category 3 exception for open-air assemblies; no altitude threshold overrides the regulatory prohibition on Cat 3 flight over such gatherings.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.text: A remote pilot with a Category 3 Declaration of Compliance wants to fly over workers at an industrial facility. The facility is an enclosed yard with a locked perimeter fence; access is restricted to credentialed employees who have been briefed that sUAS operations occur on site. Under 14 CFR Part 107, does this scenario permit Category 3 flight over the workers?

answers.text: Yes, because the operation takes place in a controlled or restricted-access site where all persons present are on notice that sUAS operations may occur
Yes, but only if each worker signs a written liability waiver acknowledging the risks before the operation begins
No, Category 3 operations over workers always require a certificate of waiver regardless of site access controls
No, Category 3 may only be conducted in Class G airspace below 200 ft AGL regardless of site configuration

explanations.a: Under 14 CFR 107.125, a Category 3 operation may be conducted if the operation is within a controlled or restricted-access site where all human beings on the ground are on notice that sUAS operations may occur; a credentialed, briefed, fenced facility meets this criterion.
explanations.b: Written liability waivers are not the regulatory mechanism for Category 3 compliance; site access control and notice to all present persons is the standard.
explanations.c: Category 3 operations in a controlled/restricted-access site do not require a certificate of waiver; the Declaration of Compliance and site conditions satisfy the regulatory requirements.
explanations.d: Airspace class and altitude are independent requirements; no Category-specific altitude or airspace rule limits Cat 3 to 200 ft AGL in Class G.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.text: An sUAS manufacturer wants to offer a drone that remote pilots can operate over people under Category 4, allowing greater operational flexibility than Categories 1 through 3. What is the primary regulatory requirement that sets Category 4 apart from the other categories?

answers.text: Category 4 requires a Declaration of Compliance with a higher injury severity threshold than Category 3
The sUAS must have an airworthiness certificate issued under 14 CFR Part 21
Category 4 requires the remote pilot to hold a commercial remote pilot certificate with an over-people endorsement
The sUAS must demonstrate at least 500 hours of accident-free flight testing before Category 4 certification

explanations.a: Category 4 does not use the Declaration of Compliance or injury severity framework; it relies on a Part 21 airworthiness certificate, which is a fundamentally different compliance pathway.
explanations.b: Under 14 CFR 107.130, a Category 4 operation requires the sUAS to have an airworthiness certificate issued under 14 CFR Part 21, such as a standard airworthiness certificate or a special airworthiness certificate.
explanations.c: There is no over-people endorsement for remote pilots in Part 107; the aircraft's airworthiness certificate is the qualifying document for Category 4.
explanations.d: Part 107 does not impose a flight-hour accident-free testing requirement for Category 4 qualification; the airworthiness certificate issued under Part 21 is the determining credential.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.text: A remote pilot is operating a Category 4 sUAS over people at a public event. Unlike other categories, Category 4 does not use the Declaration of Compliance framework. Under 14 CFR Part 107, how does the remote PIC determine and apply the correct operating limitations for a Category 4 over-people flight?

answers.text: The remote PIC applies the standard Part 107 operating limitations for all sUAS, including the 87-knot groundspeed and 400-ft AGL ceiling
The remote PIC uses the most restrictive of the Category 2 and Category 3 operating limitation sets as the governing standard
The remote PIC follows the operating limitations contained in or developed specifically for the aircraft's FAA-accepted airworthiness certificate
The remote PIC selects their own operating limitations based on the manufacturer's recommended performance data and current weather conditions

explanations.a: Standard Part 107 operating limitations still apply as a baseline, but Category 4 operations over people must additionally comply with the limitations established by the aircraft's airworthiness certificate.
explanations.b: Category 4 does not reference or combine Category 2 and Category 3 limitation sets; its governing standard is the airworthiness certificate and associated operating limitations.
explanations.c: Under 14 CFR 107.130, a Category 4 remote PIC must operate the sUAS in accordance with the operating limitations established by the FAA as part of the airworthiness certification process under Part 21.
explanations.d: The remote PIC may not self-select operating limitations for Category 4 over-people operations; the FAA-accepted airworthiness limitations are the governing standard and are not discretionary.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.keyword: sustained flight over moving vehicles categories permitted
questions.text: A production company wants to film a car chase scene by flying an sUAS over the moving vehicles on a closed course that is not a controlled or restricted-access site and is not an open-air assembly area. Under Part 107, which sUAS categories may conduct sustained flight over the moving vehicles in this scenario?

answers.text: Any category, because moving vehicle operations are unrestricted under Part 107 when the vehicles are enclosed
Only Category 4 sUAS, because the airworthiness certificate provides the necessary risk mitigation for vehicle proximity
Only Category 3 sUAS with a Declaration of Compliance and controlled-access confirmation from local authorities
Category 1 and Category 2 sUAS, which may conduct sustained flight over moving vehicles in areas that are not controlled/restricted-access sites and not open-air assemblies

explanations.a: Not all categories are permitted to fly over moving vehicles outside of controlled-access sites; the permission is category-specific.
explanations.b: Category 4 is not the only authorized category; Categories 1 and 2 may fly over moving vehicles in non-controlled, non-open-assembly areas.
explanations.c: Category 3 requires a controlled or restricted-access site or satisfaction of the non-sustained-direct-overflight condition to fly over people; it cannot fly sustained over moving vehicles in non-controlled areas.
explanations.d: Under 14 CFR 107.145, Category 1 and Category 2 sUAS may conduct sustained flight over moving vehicles in an area that is not a controlled or restricted-access site and not an open-air assembly.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.keyword: Category 3 moving vehicles controlled access only
questions.text: Using a Category 3 sUAS with a valid Declaration of Compliance, a remote pilot wants to fly sustained over moving delivery trucks making rounds through a mixed residential and commercial neighborhood. The neighborhood is open to the public and not a controlled or restricted-access area. Under Part 107, is this Category 3 flight over the moving trucks permitted?

answers.text: No, Category 3 sUAS may only conduct sustained flight over moving vehicles within a controlled or restricted-access site where all persons are on notice of sUAS operations
Yes, because moving vehicles provide a physical barrier between people and the sUAS, reducing injury risk below the Category 3 threshold
Yes, provided the sUAS speed does not exceed the maximum speed of the trucks being followed during the operation
No, but the pilot may obtain a certificate of waiver specifically for sustained flight over moving vehicles in residential areas

explanations.a: Under 14 CFR 107.145 and 107.125, Category 3 operations over moving vehicles require the flight to take place in a controlled or restricted-access site where all persons are on notice; an open public neighborhood does not qualify.
explanations.b: Vehicle enclosure does not reduce the regulatory category requirements; the site access and notice conditions still apply to Category 3.
explanations.c: Matching vehicle speed is not a regulatory condition that permits Category 3 sustained flight over moving vehicles outside a controlled-access area.
explanations.d: While a waiver could theoretically authorize deviation from certain rules, Part 107 does not describe a specific waiver pathway for this exact scenario as a standard operational option; the correct answer is the site access requirement.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.text: A major sporting event attracts 50,000 fans to an outdoor stadium with open sections. A remote pilot holding Category 3 and Category 2 Declarations of Compliance wants to fly aerial photography over the crowd. Which of these category options may be used for sustained flight directly over the open-air spectator assembly?

answers.text: Category 3 only, because its higher injury tolerance threshold makes it suitable for densely populated outdoor events
Either Category 2 or Category 3, because both categories allow over-people operations with a Declaration of Compliance
Neither Category 2 nor Category 3, because both prohibit operations over open-air assemblies of human beings
Category 2 only, because Category 3 is limited to controlled-access sites and Category 2 has no open-assembly restriction

explanations.a: Category 3 explicitly prohibits operations over open-air assemblies under 107.135; a higher energy threshold does not override this prohibition.
explanations.b: Holding a Declaration of Compliance for both categories does not authorize over-assembly flight; both categories explicitly prohibit flight over open-air assemblies.
explanations.c: Under 14 CFR 107.135, no person may conduct a Category 3 operation over an open-air assembly; Category 2 similarly prohibits operations over open-air assemblies of human beings.
explanations.d: Category 2 also prohibits operations over open-air assemblies, not just Category 3; neither category may be used for sustained flight over the open spectator crowd.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.keyword: Declaration of Compliance purpose and content
questions.text: A drone manufacturer prepares to submit a Declaration of Compliance for a new sUAS intended for Category 2 over-people operations. The Declaration of Compliance is submitted to the FAA DroneZone. Which statement accurately describes what a Declaration of Compliance must assert?

answers.text: The Declaration of Compliance certifies that the sUAS has received a Part 21 type certificate and been tested by an FAA-designated airworthiness representative
The Declaration of Compliance states that the sUAS meets the applicable injury severity and design requirements for the declared category, based on an FAA-accepted means of compliance
The Declaration of Compliance is a waiver application that must be re-approved by the FAA every 24 months to remain valid
The Declaration of Compliance requires a minimum of 1,000 flight test hours documented by an independent test agency before submission

explanations.a: A Part 21 type certificate and designated airworthiness representative are Category 4 requirements; Categories 2 and 3 use the Declaration of Compliance pathway, not Part 21 certification.
explanations.b: Under 14 CFR 107.120 and 107.125, the Declaration of Compliance is a document in which the manufacturer declares that the sUAS meets the FAA-accepted injury severity limit and design requirements (such as no exposed laceration parts) for the applicable category, using an FAA-accepted means of compliance.
explanations.c: The Declaration of Compliance is a manufacturer's declaration, not a waiver application; it does not require recurring FAA reapproval on a fixed schedule.
explanations.d: There is no 1,000-flight-hour independent testing requirement for a Declaration of Compliance; the document is based on design compliance with FAA-accepted standards, not accumulated flight hours.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.objective: 2.7 Category 1 no Declaration of Compliance required
questions.keyword: Category 1 exemption from Declaration of Compliance
questions.text: A remote pilot compares the regulatory requirements for Category 1 and Category 2 operations and notices a key documentation difference. Under 14 CFR Part 107, which document is required for Category 2 but NOT required for Category 1 over-people operations?

answers.text: A written authorization from the airport closest to the area of operation, regardless of airspace class
A certificate of waiver from the FAA authorizing the over-people flight for the specific operation date
A Declaration of Compliance documenting that the sUAS meets applicable injury severity and design requirements
A current instrument rating endorsement on the remote pilot certificate for complex over-people operations

explanations.a: Airport authorization is an airspace issue unrelated to the over-people category documentation requirements.
explanations.b: A certificate of waiver is not required for Category 1 or Category 2 standard over-people operations; waivers are for deviating from Part 107 rules.
explanations.c: Under 14 CFR 107.115 and 107.120, Category 1 does not require a Declaration of Compliance; Category 2 requires the remote PIC to have one available during the operation.
explanations.d: Instrument ratings are a manned aviation concept; no such endorsement exists for remote pilot certificates in the context of over-people operations.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.keyword: Category 3 participant vs non-participant sustained overflight
questions.text: A film production crew uses a Category 3 sUAS on a closed set. The camera operators, director, and other crew members are all participants in the operation and have been briefed accordingly. Can the Category 3 sUAS conduct sustained flight directly over the participating crew members?

answers.text: Yes, Part 107 over-people restrictions apply only to non-participant human beings; the remote PIC may conduct sustained flight over participants in the operation
No, Category 3 restricts all sustained over-people flight to controlled sites regardless of whether the persons below are participants
Yes, but only if each participating crew member wears a hard hat meeting OSHA impact protection standards
No, Category 3 prohibits sustained flight over any person, including participants, who is closer than 25 feet to the aircraft during operation

explanations.a: Under 14 CFR 107.110 and 107.120, the restrictions on operations over human beings apply to persons who are not participants in the operation; participants who are aware of and part of the sUAS operation are not subject to the same restrictions.
explanations.b: The participant/non-participant distinction is fundamental to Subpart D; briefed crew members on a closed set are participants and the category restrictions regarding non-participants do not apply to them.
explanations.c: OSHA hard hat requirements are not a Part 107 operational standard; participant status, not personal protective equipment, determines the applicability of over-people restrictions.
explanations.d: Part 107 does not impose a minimum horizontal or vertical separation distance between Category 3 sUAS and participants in the operation.

questions.name: Operations Over People
questions.text: A Category 3 remote pilot wants to operate over workers at an outdoor site that has not been designated as a formal controlled or restricted-access area. No open-air assembly is involved. Under 14 CFR Part 107, what alternative condition would permit this Category 3 operation without a controlled-access site?

answers.text: The flight must be limited to a single pass over each worker at a minimum of 200 ft AGL with no hovering
The remote pilot must issue a formal Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) to alert workers of the sUAS presence
The remote pilot must obtain signed consent from a majority of the non-participant workers before beginning the operation
The sUAS does not maintain sustained flight directly over any individual non-participant; the operation avoids continued presence above any single person who is not a participant

explanations.a: A minimum altitude of 200 ft for a single pass is not the alternative condition specified in Part 107 for Category 3 operations outside controlled-access sites.
explanations.b: NOTAMs are airspace notification tools, not a mechanism for satisfying Category 3 non-controlled-site operational requirements.
explanations.c: Written consent from workers is not the regulatory alternative to a controlled-access site under Category 3 requirements.
explanations.d: Under 14 CFR 107.125, a Category 3 operation may occur outside a controlled or restricted-access site if the sUAS does not maintain sustained flight directly over any human being who is not a participant in the operation; avoiding stationary overflight of non-participants satisfies this alternative condition.
